audits.title: Documentation of neurovascular assessment in fracture patients in a tertiary care hospital: A retrospective review.
audits.standard: British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) on documentation of neurovascular assessment; no target stated
audits.setting: Tertiary care hospital / major trauma centre; emergency department and orthopaedic clerking of patients admitted to trauma wards with acute fractures

cycle1.result: ED notes: no neurovascular documentation 17 (22.1%), 'NVI' only 30 (38.9%), specific documentation 30 (38.9%). Orthopaedic notes: no documentation 3 (3.8%), NVI only 16 (20.7%), specific documentation 58 (75.3%). Post-manipulation in ED (n=19): no documentation 12 (63.2%), specific 6 (31.6%).

audits.intervention: Posters in trauma units, generic educational emails to all ED and orthopaedic doctors, and consultant-led joint ED and orthopaedic teaching sessions.

cycle2.result: ED notes: no documentation 6 (7.3%), NVI only 8 (9.7%), specific documentation 68 (82.9%). Orthopaedic notes: no documentation 0 (0%), NVI only 4 (3.6%), specific documentation 74 (90.2%). Post-manipulation in ED (n=22): no documentation 7 (31.8%), NVI only 4 (18.1%), specific 11 (50%).

audits.other_findings: Post-manipulation neurovascular documentation remained poor, with nearly a third of manipulated patients still having none. Patients clerked by the project authors were excluded from the re-audit.
audits.citation: Faraz A, Qureshi AI, Noah H Khan M, Yawar B, Malik M, Saghir M, et al.. Documentation of neurovascular assessment in fracture patients in a tertiary care hospital: A retrospective review. Ann Med Surg (Lond). 2022;79:103935. doi:10.1016/j.amsu.2022.103935. PMID: 35860148.

audits.title: Management of displaced supracondylar fractures in children and adherence to the BOAST guideline- experience in a District General Hospital, UK.
audits.setting: North Manchester General Hospital; district general hospital

cycle1.result: ED: capillary refill 65%, radial pulse 59.2%, individual nerve function 37.9%; pre-op nerve function 42.7%; 2 mm K-wires 53.3%; post-op pulse/CRT 27.2%, nerve function 9.7%

audits.intervention: Supracondylar fracture assessment proforma and focused educational sessions

cycle2.result: ED: capillary refill 95.5% (p=0.0038), radial pulse 95.5% (p=0.0009), nerve function 72.7% (p=0.0040); pre-op nerve function 50%; 2 mm K-wires 89.5%; post-op pulse/CRT 54.2%, nerve function 50%

audits.other_findings: Medial wire technique documentation rose from 82.9% to 100% and post-fixation stability from 42.7% to 89.5%; pre-op nerve documentation stayed low.
audits.citation: Jain S, Loganathan D, Ahmed A, Mohan R, Sheikh M. Management of displaced supracondylar fractures in children and adherence to the BOAST guideline- experience in a District General Hospital, UK. J Clin Orthop Trauma. 2023;45:102276. doi:10.1016/j.jcot.2023.102276. PMID: 37994354.

audits.title: Improving Patient Care and Clinical Services: Compliance With the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines for Neurological and Vascular Assessment of Acute Fractures.
audits.standard: BOAST Peripheral Nerve Injury guideline (December 2021): documentation of specific nerve and arterial status; target 100%
audits.setting: Russell Hall Hospital (Trauma and Orthopaedic admissions)

cycle1.result: Any NV documentation 43/49 (87.8%); detailed neurological findings 19/49 (38.8%); detailed vascular findings 13/49 (26.5%).

audits.intervention: Single educational awareness presentation on the consequences of poor NV assessment (May 2024).

cycle2.result: Any NV documentation 47/48 (97.9%) (p = 0.053); detailed neurological findings 26/48 (54.2%) (p = 0.129); detailed vascular findings 22/48 (45.8%) (p = 0.048).

audits.other_findings: Many entries still used the nonspecific phrase 'NV intact' rather than nerve-specific and arterial details.
audits.citation: Mussab RM, Ahmad I, Sohail R, Jany TJ, Anil Kumar VR. Improving Patient Care and Clinical Services: Compliance With the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines for Neurological and Vascular Assessment of Acute Fractures. Cureus. 2025;17(12):e98439. doi:10.7759/cureus.98439. PMID: 41492587.
